_comment: Screen shaders: the full-screen post-process passes offered by the pause menu's Shaders page. shader_overlay.gd builds one layer per entry in this order - a later entry draws over an earlier one - and settings_menu.gd turns each param into a row under the shader's own heading. 'id' keys this shader's saved state in user://settings.cfg (section [shaders], keys '<id>_enabled' and '<id>_<param key>'), and 'enabled' is what a fresh install starts with. Param types: 'float' reads min/max/step (a slider row, with an optional 'suffix' shown after the value) and 'bool' is a toggle row. The uniform each param drives is the param's own 'key', so a shader's uniforms, this list and the saved keys all carry the same names. Lengths a pass measures in its own picture pixels say so in their label: the CRT's mask pitch is picture pixels per phosphor triad, not frame pixels. Where a param's unit is the screen rather than the picture, its label says that too: the CRT's 'picture_scale' is screen pixels per dot of the picture, not a count of lines, so a dot is always a whole number of the screen's pixels and one value means the same thing at every window size. On a 960-pixel-tall window the values are 1x (960 lines, the frame itself), 2x (480), 3x (320), 4x (240 - the raster of a late-90s set), 5x, 6x (160) and 8x (120).
